380YE Autumn Equinox Imperial elections.d: New senators took office for Kahraman, Semmerholm, Casinea, Upwold and Volodmartz. Incumbents were returned for Tassato, Therunin, Morrow and Hahnmark. Yelislaveta Syrnova Vlanich became Senator for Miekarova after the previous holder was executed. Generals were chosen for six armies, four of them incumbents. The Synod chose new Cardinals of Loyalty and Pride, gatekeepers, virtue inquisitors and a Dean of Laroc Cathedral. Bourse seats were allocated, with the Fortress of Salt going for 600 thrones. The Great Mine of Briante and an unnamed Sermersuaq region still needed allocating, and several posts were left unfilled. The page was updated throughout the event.

n.Dawn: Escalados de Carsenere became Senator for Semmerholm. Dawn also gained Rodrigo Whittington as Virtue Inquisitor of Courage and Lady Eleanor de Rondell as Dean of Laroc Cathedral.
n.Highguard: Barrabas became Senator for Casinea. Ephrael of Highguard was returned as Virtue Inquisitor of Pride, and Brother Luke of the Shattered Tower kept the post of Master of Ice and Darkness.
n.Navarr: Caerwyn Summer Crow was returned as Senator for Therunin, and Corwin Leafstalker of Navarr became Virtue Inquisitor of Loyalty.
n.The Brass Coast: Qusay i Kalamar i Guerra was elected Senator for Kahraman.
n.The League: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato kept his seat for Tassato. League citizens also took Synod posts: Oberon Di Tassato as Cardinal of Loyalty, and Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato returned as Gatekeeper of Pride.
n.The Marches: Henry Ward became Senator for Upwold. Tess of the Marches became Gatekeeper of Loyalty, and Silas Merrick was named Civilian Commissioner for The Marches.
n.Urizen: Ariadne was returned as Senator for Morrow.
n.Varushka: Vuk the wolf-eater became Senator for Volodmartz and Yelislaveta Syrnova Vlanich took Miekarova after its previous senator was executed. Elka Nadayanova Gremani of Varushka became Cardinal of Pride.
n.Wintermark: Hengest Dun was returned as Senator for Hahnmark, and Tyr Brenna was named Civilian Commissioner for Wintermark.

t.Casinea: Casinea elected Barrabas as its senator.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark returned its incumbent senator, Hengest Dun.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman elected Qusay i Kalamar i Guerra as its senator.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova's previous senator had been executed, and Yelislaveta Syrnova Vlanich was elected to the seat.
t.Morrow: Morrow returned its incumbent senator, Ariadne.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm elected Escalados de Carsenere as its senator.
t.Tassato: Tassato returned its incumbent senator, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato.
t.Therunin: Therunin returned its incumbent senator, Caerwyn Summer Crow.
t.Upwold: Upwold elected Henry Ward as its senator.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz elected Vuk the wolf-eater as its senator.

380YE Autumn Equinox winds of fortune.d: An unnatural blizzard besieged the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, and a conjunction of the Web and the Chain strengthened emotional bonds. A Marcher friar urged citizens not to sell treasure to the Bourse, and a goat-footed spirit troubled the Imperial Orcs and Wintermark. Heralds of Lashonar sang against war, the Congregation of the First Empress grew, and mysterious hunters raided Sermersuaq. The orcs of the Great Forest entered Therunin as guests, and strange blessed weapons emerged from the fallen Mournwold. Sermersuaq's mithril mine neared completion and the Great Pits of Ennerlund resumed production. Tassato's Penumbral Veil faded, while Optarion's fortification and Holberg's lands remained under threat.

n.Dawn: Heralds of Lashonar visited Dawn singing songs of sorrow that cast war as a horror to be avoided. Dawn is also tagged in the storms and rumoured beasts troubling the Semmerlak.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: their earlier sabotage is blamed for the spreading Holberg marshes, and they are noted as past conquerors of the Great Pits of Ennerlund; the stars have also vanished over the Barrens.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: they are noted as remaining a significant threat in Spiral despite its reclamation.
n.Highguard: The Congregation of the First Empress, and the influence of the living Paragon Yael of Felix's Watch, continued to grow. Highguard's claim to Empress Giselle's sarcophagus remained unresolved, and the nation was tagged in the Mournwold developments.
n.Imperial Orcs: A bizarre shaggy beast seen around Pakaanan's Pass carried a cryptic, unsettling message for the Imperial Orcs. The stars vanished over Skarsind, and the nation was tagged in the Mournwold developments.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: they are not named, but the Mournwold they hold is described as the lost Marcher territory from which eerie blessed weapons and strange ideas are emerging.
n.Navarr: The orcs of the Great Forest entered Therunin as guests of the Navarr, and intense negotiation is needed over what this means for the future.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Segura is listed among the territories whose stars have vanished.
n.The League: Celebrations marked Empress Lisabetta's coronation, and the Penumbral Veil over Tassato finally faded. The League's dispute with Highguard over Empress Giselle's sarcophagus continued, and Holberg faced costly choices as its marshes spread.
n.The Marches: Friar Alyn of Hay toured the Marches urging citizens not to sell treasure to the Imperial Bourse. Eerie blessed weapons and strange ideas began emerging from the fallen Mournwold, and the stars vanished over Bregasland.
n.Urizen: Spiral was reclaimed for the Empire, though the Grendel remain a threat there. The Court of the White Fountain in Optarion continued to crumble under a winter curse.
n.Varushka: An unnatural blizzard besieged the castle on the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, while the Semmerlak was wracked by night storms and rumoured beasts. The stars vanished over Volodmartz, Karsk and Miekarova.
n.Wintermark: A strange spirit troubled the Winterfolk around Northspires, and mysterious hunters began bloodless raids in Sermersuaq. The new Sermersuaq mithril mine neared completion, and the Senate may decide whether it becomes an Imperial or a Wintermark national resource.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: there are said to be developments with the eerie fog on the bay, detailed elsewhere.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: it is listed among the territories where the stars have vanished.
t.Hahnmark: A bizarre, shaggy spirit was occasionally sighted around Northspires, bearing an unsettling message for the Winterfolk and their orc neighbours.
t.Holberg: The marshes continued to spread, turning Rebeshof into marsh and permanently cutting Holberg's farm production by 18 rings. The Senate may pay 80 wains of weirwood and 20 Thrones either to save Ennerlund or to cultivate the marsh for herbs; the stars have also vanished here.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: its marshes are the benchmark for healing herbs that a cultivated Holberg marsh might nearly rival.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: it is listed among the territories where the stars have vanished.
t.Miekarova: The stars vanished over Miekarova, and an unnaturally strong blizzard roared around the castle on the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun while leaving the vale of Volchitrava untouched.
t.Mournwold: Though the territory has fallen, eerie blessed weapons and strange ideas are emerging from parts of it. These have implications for the campaign, especially for the five armies camped in Tassato.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: it is listed among the territories where the stars have vanished.
t.Redoubt: The Court of the White Fountain in Optarion continued to crumble under a winter curse, opposed by magicians from the Spire of the Auric Horizon.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: it is listed among the territories where the stars have vanished.
t.Sermersuaq: Strangely dressed hunters gathered on the northern shores of Atkonaroq and began raids in which almost nobody was harmed and nothing of note was taken. The new mithril mine is completed at the Autumn Equinox, and the stars have vanished here.
t.Skarsind: The stars vanished over Skarsind, and a strange goat-footed spirit was repeatedly sighted around Pakaanan's Pass.
t.Spiral: The territory was reclaimed for the Empire, though the Grendel remain a significant threat there, and the civil service began reviewing opportunities in it.
t.Tassato: The Penumbral Veil that had twisted Tassato's night sky for a year faded entirely before the Equinox. The five armies camped here face implications from events in the Mournwold.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: it is listed among the territories where the stars have vanished.
t.The Semmerlak: The lake lay windless by day but was struck by violent storms at night, with rumours of unnatural beasts preying on fisherfolk, sailors and those who stray near its waters.
t.Therunin: The orcs of the Great Forest entered Therunin as guests of the Navarr, raising pressing questions about the territory's future.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: it is listed among the territories where the stars have vanished.

r.Hahnmark/Northspires: The bizarre, shaggy beast was occasionally sighted around Northspires.
r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Great Pits of Ennerlund produced their first Imperial mithril since the Druj conquest, with the seat going to auction. Unless the Senate funds new dikes, the region will become a marsh by the Winter Solstice, raising the Pits' upkeep by 2 Thrones a season.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: Large sections of Rebeshof reverted to sodden marsh, and the region was officially declared a marsh. It is now too late to prevent this.
r.Holberg/The Morass: The marshes of the Morass continued to spread unchecked after last season's enchantment, swallowing Rebeshof and threatening Ennerlund.
r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: An unnaturally strong, unrelenting blizzard roared around the castle on the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, leaving the vale and people of Volchitrava untouched.
r.Redoubt/Optarion: The Court of the White Fountain's fiery plume guttered and its white stone cracked under a winter curse. If the curse has not run its course by the Winter Solstice, it may prove permanent.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: There were multiple sightings of a bizarre, shaggy spirit around the pass, bearing a cryptic, unsettling message for the Imperial Orcs.

380YE Autumn Equinox winds of war.d: The Black Thorns used terror tactics and risen Navarr dead to drive the Jotun from southern Liathaven, liberating Beacon Point and advancing into Western Scout. In Kahraman more than thirty-five thousand Imperial troops retook Serra Briante and the Great Mine, but the glacial citadel of Cathan Canae kept the Jotun in Serra Damata; about ten thousand warriors on both sides were lost. The Mournwold fell entirely, Orchard's Watch and Overton included. The Freeborn Storm lost nearly a fifth of the navy at Rebekah's Leap and the Pharos. The Citadel Guard took over half of Tamarbode. The Golden Axe repelled an unliving horde in Astolat, and Druj envoys offered to negotiate the Line.

n.Dawn: The Gryphon's Pride and Golden Sun took just over half of the Carmine Fields and received a Druj offer to negotiate the Line. The Hounds of Glory led the vanguard in Kahraman, and Astolat was defended against an unliving horde.
n.Druj: The Druj returned to the Barrens and exterminated the Rahvin, after half the Black Wind sought peace with them. Their envoys now wait in the Bitter Strand for a Senate diplomat to negotiate the Line before the Equinox ends.
n.Grendel: An armada more than twice the size of the Freeborn Storm defeated it at Rebekah's Leap and again off Necropolis. In Spiral the Grendel stood on the defensive, holding Apstrus, Apulus and Screed.
n.Highguard: The Valiant Pegasus could only watch the naval defeat off Necropolis, and the Granite Pillar fought in the lost defence of Orchard's Watch. The Seventh Wave resupplied in Sarvos, while Urizen forces pushed into Llofir's Tamarbode in Reikos.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm helped liberate Serra Briante. The Tusks and Winter Sun shaped the Mournwold defence but were forced out with the other defenders, and a fleet from Skarsind sailed with the Freeborn Storm.
n.Jotun: The Jotun conquered the whole Mournwold, Orchard's Watch and the Singing Caves included, and still hold Serra Damata with Cathan Canae's aid. They lost Serra Briante, abandoned southern Liathaven in fear of the Navarr and withdrew from Kallavesa.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns and their unliving allies liberated Beacon Point and are close to freeing all of southern Liathaven. The Jotun executed nearly a hundred Navarr prisoners at Briante, and the Great Forest orcs arrived in Therunin as Navarr guests.
n.The Brass Coast: Serra Briante and its Great Mine were retaken, and the Senate may now make the mine a Brass Coast national seat. Nearly a fifth of the Imperial navy was lost when the Freeborn Storm was defeated by the Grendel.
n.The League: The Seventh Wave searched Sarvos for a spy network without success, and the Mournwold's defenders retreated into Tassato. Holberg is recalled only for the moving trees that once besieged it.
n.The Marches: After three centuries the Mournwold was lost to the Jotun: Overton fell and Marcher rebels who had broken the thrall's oath now face likely execution. Bregasland, guarded by its citadel, saw no orc incursion.
n.Urizen: The Citadel Guard recaptured a little over half of Tamarbode against Llofir's supernatural defenders. Urizen magicians aided the Mournwold defenders, and the first naval battle was fought off Redoubt.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe drove an unliving horde from Astolat but lost some two hundred soldiers, received no resupply and lost the benefit of Brotherhood of Tian. The horde itself came out of Karsk.
n.Wintermark: Jotun forces advancing into Kallavesa turned back, though a beachhead in West March remains. Wintermark forces supported the burial truce in Kahraman, and Winterfolk boarders crippled a Grendel warship.

t.Astolat: An unliving horde attacked near Weaving before the Golden Axe, Dawnish witches and the Castle of Thorns garrison drove it back into Weirwater.
t.Bay of Catazar: The unnatural fog persisted as rival Imperial and Grendel fleets came to share these waters; the Imperial Treasury's Auditor has prepared a report on the situation for the Admiral.
t.Bregasland: A magical citadel again guarded the marshes, but no orc forces entered Bregasland.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the trees of Tamarbode are compared with the mobile trees that once besieged Holberg.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: Jotun warbands fleeing Liathaven retreated into Hordalant and Reinos.
t.Kahraman: Imperial armies liberated Serra Briante and the Great Mine and now dominate over half the Damatian hills, but the Jotun still hold out beneath Cathan Canae's citadel after a campaign that cost about ten thousand warriors.
t.Kallavesa: A magical citadel protected the sacred lakes, and the advancing Jotun paused and marched back west, leaving only a beachhead in West March.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: the unliving army that attacked Astolat is described as the haunted legion out of Karsk.
t.Liathaven: The Black Thorns liberated Beacon Point and gained ground in Western Scout, and are on course to free all of southern Liathaven and make it contested again by Winter.
t.Mournwold: The Jotun took the entire territory, including Overton, the Singing Caves and Orchard's Watch, so the Sheriff of Overton sinecure now yields nothing.
t.Necropolis: The Battle of the Pharos was fought below the cliffs and lost by the Empire; neither navy now fully controls these waters.
t.Redoubt: The Battle of Rebekah's Leap, the first major naval clash with the Grendel, was fought off Redoubt and ended in an Imperial retreat.
t.Reikos: Outside Tamarbode the transforming magic is fading and fresh greenery has replaced the ruins, while the Citadel Guard has recaptured just over half of Tamarbode itself.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun retreated towards Reinos from both Liathaven and Kahraman.
t.Sarvos: The Seventh Wave guarded against seaborne threats and resupplied unimpeded, while its scouts searched without success for an alleged spy network.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: a Red Wind Corsairs order urges the troops to 'remember Segura'.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the unliving army turned aside at the last minute rather than entering Semmerholm.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: one independent fleet sailing with the Freeborn Storm had a captain who calls Skarsind home.
t.Spiral: Spiral stays Imperial in an uneasy standoff, with the Empire holding four regions and the Grendel three, and the Black Plateau has grown quieter.
t.Tassato: The Mournwold's defenders retreated into Tassato, and the heroism shown at the Summer Solstice may have prevented a Jotun beachhead here.
t.The Barrens: Dawn took just over half of the Carmine Fields, the Rahvin were wiped out by the Druj, the Great Forest and half the Black Wind left, and a Druj presence of unknown size has arrived.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: the unliving army that attacked Astolat had earlier emerged from the Semmerlak.
t.Therunin: Some two thousand Great Forest orcs, with much of their people and some briar humans, camped in the Lower Tarn Valley as guests of the Navarr.
t.Weirwater: The unliving horde crossed Weirwater to attack Astolat and is now camped in its south-western woods, far from any major settlement.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: The Fort Braydon garrison was cut off from the main Imperial force, but the Jotun made no attempt to invade the region.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: The Jotun aimed their strength at conquering Gambit, but the Imperial offensive blunted the push.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The Jotun sought to take Jade Range, but their advance was halted when the Empire went on the attack.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: After weeks of bloody fighting the Empire drove the Jotun out and recovered the Great Mine. Inside Briante town it found nearly a hundred executed Navarr prisoners.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: The Empire now dominates over half the Damatian hills, but Cathan Canae's citadel killed some two hundred attackers and keeps the Jotun foothold secure.
r.Liathaven/Beacon Point: Beacon Point was liberated by the Black Thorns within six weeks of the Solstice.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: This is an opportunity rather than an event: once southern Liathaven is free, the Navarr could strike into West Ranging to cut the Jotun supply lines into the Mournwold.
r.Liathaven/Western Scout: The Black Thorns made significant gains here, and the Jotun held their own by day but died in the dark by night.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Orchard's Watch, Overton and the Singing Caves fell to the Jotun, whose people will now be offered the Choice.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Mentioned in passing: Jotun campfires spread across Ore Hills before the assault on Orchard's Watch.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun host camped across Southmoor before the final assault.
r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: The ruins of Chalcis Mount are gone, replaced by flourishing untouched greenery as the transforming magic fades.
r.Reikos/Haros Water: The Druj-era ruins of Haros Water have vanished beneath fast-growing but largely normal forest.
r.Reikos/Longshire: Longshire's ruins are gone and fresh greenery now flourishes in their place.
r.Reikos/Riverwatch: The ruins of Riverwatch have been replaced by new growth as the Spring magic recedes.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Spore-choked forest and hostile creatures slowed the Citadel Guard, which recaptured just over half the region amid growing resistance; it may finish by Winter if Llofir does not respond.
r.Spiral/Ankra: Ankra is defended by Imperial armies in the standoff with the Grendel.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: Apstrus remains in Grendel hands and is fervently defended.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Apulus remains held and defended by the Grendel.
r.Spiral/Ateri: Ateri is held by Imperial armies including the Eastern Sky, Green Shield and Northern Eagle.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Cinion is one of the four regions defended by Imperial forces.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Ossuary and its mithril mine, captured from the Grendel at the Summer Solstice, are held by the Empire.
r.Spiral/Screed: The Grendel hold Screed, where the Black Plateau appears to be settling down though it has not fallen entirely silent.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: The last Imperial soldiers were harried out of the Mournwold back across the border towards Tassato Mestra.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Druj envoys await a Senate diplomatic party on the eastern banks of the Kepahitân River, and scouting parties sent here failed to return.
r.The Barrens/Farweald: Mentioned in passing: the Rahvin used Farweald's magical defences in their failing resistance against Dawn.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest orcs left the Barrens through Hope's Rest into Therunin.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Half the Black Wind crossed the river east of the Saltmarsh to make peace with the Druj, and errants reported some five thousand orcs camped by the marshes.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: A great camp was raised here for the Great Forest orcs, who were welcomed by representatives of Therunin's steadings and stridings.
r.Weirwater/Hawksmoor: The unliving horde marched west through Hawksmoor on its way to attack Astolat.
r.Weirwater/Weirmoor: The unliving army passed through Weirmoor towards Astolat and later retreated into the woods of south-western Weirwater.

Accept Sarcophan Delves treaty.d: The treaty, signed by Imperial Consul Aureliana Perpetua Nicasia Saverio di Sarvos, Ambassador Thanmir Hrafn and Edwin Vandersaar, offered 24 wains of white granite a season at 32, 29 and 26 crowns for successive batches of eight. It would hold while neither party was at war with the other, with quantity and price open to renegotiation after a year. A Senate-appointed minister would oversee purchases. Proposed by Miaren and seconded by Zenith, the motion passed. The Bedelaar-Huisbaas ratified it, and work on the docks in Redoubt could begin after the Winter Solstice 380YE. Construction would cost 40 wains of weirwood, 10 of white granite and 12 thrones 4 crowns, and take three months. The civil service sought the proposing Senator's guidance on whether the overseeing title would be national or Imperial.

n.Urizen: Urizen was to host the new cargo dock and ministerial offices in its territory of Redoubt. If the overseeing title were made national, Urizeni citizens might appoint the minister using their traditional methods.

t.Redoubt: The Senator intended to build the cargo docks and ministerial offices for unloading Sarcophan white granite in Redoubt, with work able to begin after the Winter Solstice 380YE.

Allocate the Great Mine of Briante.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Kahraman and seconded by the senator for Feroz. It allocated the Great Mine of Briante, a bourse seat located in Kahraman, as an Imperial position, and the Senate passed it. As a result, the Great Mine of Briante remained Imperial and was due to be auctioned for a reduced term at the Winter Solstice 380YE.

n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast senators for Kahraman and Feroz proposed and seconded the motion, which kept a bourse seat on Brass Coast land under Imperial control, to be auctioned rather than appointed by the nation.

t.Kahraman: The Great Mine of Briante in Kahraman remained an Imperial Bourse position, to be auctioned for a reduced term at the Winter Solstice 380YE.

Allocate the Pride of Ikka's Tears.d: The motion allocated the mithril mine that had been under construction in Sermersuaq since Winter 379YE, naming it the Pride of Ikka's Tears and making it a national position. It passed in Autumn 380YE. The seat became a national Bourse position of Wintermark, allocated by secret vote of Wintermark's military captains. Unlike the Stonefield Ice Caves, the actions a military unit has been engaging in have no bearing on the vote. The first election was set for the Winter Solstice 380YE; after that the seat is elected each Autumn, like all other mithril seats.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained a new national Bourse seat controlling a mithril mine, to be awarded by secret ballot of its military captains, first at the Winter Solstice 380YE and then each Autumn.

t.Sermersuaq: The mithril mine built in Sermersuaq since Winter 379YE was formally allocated as the Pride of Ikka's Tears, a Wintermark national Bourse position.

Allocate the Singing Caves.d: The Singing Caves in the Mournwold had recently been liberated by the heroes of the Empire, and this Autumn 380YE motion sought to make them a national position. The Marches and the League were the nations proposed, and the record states the position was assigned to the Marches. The motion was subject to the veto of the Throne. The constitutional note is written conditionally, recording that had the motion passed, the national status of the associated Bourse seat would have followed the Mournwold to whichever nation the territory was eventually assigned. This suggests the allocation may not have taken final effect.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, but they held the Mournwold at the time the Imperial Senate debated the newly liberated caves.
n.The League: The League was one of the two nations proposed to receive the Singing Caves, but the record names the Marches as the nation it was assigned to.
n.The Marches: The Marches, whose senator for Mitwold proposed the motion, were recorded as the nation assigned the Singing Caves, subject to the Throne's veto.

t.Mournwold: The Singing Caves within the Mournwold, recently liberated by Imperial heroes, were the subject of the allocation, even though the territory itself was held by the Jotun at the time.

Archive:380YE Autumn Equinox Imperial ti.d: The list named the senators for each territory, the generals of every national army, the Synod's cardinals, gatekeepers and inquisitors, the Archmagi and Grandmasters of the Conclave, and the holders of Imperial and national Bourse seats, commissions and sinecures. Several gaps stood out. The Great Mine of Briante was vacant and due to be auctioned at the Winter Solstice for a reduced term, and the Pride of Ikka's Tears was due to be elected then. The Singing Caves were back in Imperial control and awaited allocation by the Senate. The Damatian Cliffs were held by the Jotun and the Stonefield Ice Caves by the Thule. The Sheriff of Overton post was vacant after the town's loss and recovery, and the Gatekeeper of Wisdom was also vacant.

n.Dawn: Dawn held three Senate seats and four generals, including Tancred de Rondell of the Hounds of Glory, while House de Rondell also supplied the Warmage Barthol and the Cardinal of Wisdom Agnetha.
n.Highguard: Highguard held four Senate seats, three generals and a raft of Synod offices, including the Imperial Inquisitor Ephron of Adina's Charge and the Custodian of the Imperial War Memorial.
n.Imperial Orcs: The orcs had Irontide Vio as senator for Skarsind, generals of the Winter Sun and Summer Storm, and Atla as Cardinal of the Way, and held the Steel Fist and Brilliant Shore Bourse seats.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are listed as holding the Damatian Cliffs, an Imperial Bourse position.
n.Navarr: Navarr held three Senate seats and the generals of the Black Thorns and Quiet Step, with Brendan Brackensong serving as Quartermaster General of the Imperial Armies.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn held four Senate seats, the generals of the Red Wind Corsairs and Fire of the South and the admiral of the Freeborn Storm, and Zanferr i Ezmara i Erigo was Imperial Fleet Master.
n.The League: The League held the Throne through Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, four Senate seats, two generals and the cardinalships of Ambition, Loyalty and Vigilance.
n.The Marches: The Marches held three Senate seats and four generals, Tess served as Gatekeeper of Loyalty, and Robert Shanks operated Brock's Toll.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are listed as holding the Stonefield Ice Caves, a Wintermark national Bourse position.
n.Urizen: Urizen held four Senate seats and a single general, Nicassia Avicia of the Citadel Guard; Maximillian served as Conscience of the Senate and Solas as High Exorcist.
n.Varushka: Varushka held four Senate seats, the generals of the Northern Eagle and Golden Axe, and the Cardinal of Pride, Elka Nadayanova Gremani.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark held three Senate seats and two generals, but its Pride of Ikka's Tears seat was vacant and the Stonefield Ice Caves were held by the Thule.
