t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Ianthe, of Raven's Watch, is listed as senator for Necropolis.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Probus of Shattered Spire is listed as senator for Redoubt.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Balthasar, of the Suns of Couros, is listed as senator for Reikos, and the Great Forest at Reikos is held by Azazel of Ravensfell.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Alessandra Serafini is listed as senator for Sarvos.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra is listed as senator for Segura.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Escalados de Carsenere is listed as senator for Semmerholm.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Atte is listed as senator for Sermersuaq.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Irontide Vio is listed as senator for Skarsind, and Irontide T'onk as Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Tanwyn Ankarien is listed as senator for Spiral, and Maryc as Castellan of Spiral Castle.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato is listed as senator for Tassato.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Gant Archama is listed as senator for Temeschwar.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Caerwyn Summer Crow is listed as senator for Therunin.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Henry Ward is listed as senator for Upwold, The Silver Chase.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: Vuk the Wolfeater is listed as senator for Volodmartz.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Valentin Ivarovich Orzel is listed as senator for Weirwater, and the Weirwater Vales are held by Soren il Signo.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Edmundo of Endsmeet is listed as senator for Zenith.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Mentioned in passing: the Great Pits of Ennerlund are listed as held by Lukash Biessek von Temeschwar for 590 Thrones.

Castle of wind and sky.d: Since the solstice, heavy snow-laden clouds have hung over the Crag, and vindictive winds strike any magician who steps outside, while the people of the vale walk through the storms untouched. Inside, the stone protects the occupants. Ritual research continued, but magicians grew reluctant to travel there, so the Empire had to pay far higher wages than planned, doubling the college's running costs for as long as the curse lasts. Rumour held that Cathan Canae was angered because Meraud's banner hangs in the Crag's halls instead of hers, after she had been promised patronage. Possible remedies included careful diplomacy, which risked angering Meraud, or a Conclave declaration of enmity, which would break the curse.

n.Varushka: The Varushkan vale of Volchitrava now hosts a college besieged by an eternal's wrath, with a stream of strangers visiting. Its own people remained untouched by the storms and walked freely through them.

t.Miekarova: Miekarova's Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun lay under Cathan Canae's curse, and storms battered any magician who ventured outside the fortress walls.

r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: The vale of Volchitrava's fortress was wrapped in snow clouds and capricious gales aimed only at outsiders, with strange effects such as washing drying within an hour in falling snow.

Construct Dunfrith.d: Ham, son of Brigantia, lead apothecary of Dunhearth, acting with the authority of the Great Thane Tobrytan Dunning, called Spooner, had the foresters of Woodhall fell trees to create carefully placed glades near Dunhearth Hall. Plantings showed that Bladeroot, Cerulean Mazzarine, Marrowort (in glades on sites of skirmishes with the Feni), True Vervain and Imperial Roseweald would all grow there. The balanced herb sinecure, funded by Ham's family, was approved by the Civilian Commissioner using powers delegated by the Senate, at standard cost. Thanmir Hrafnar supplied 12 wains of weirwood and 24 crowns after the Autumn Equinox. Ham was proposed as overseer, but Wintermark's senators are not bound to elect him.

n.Wintermark: Once completed, Dunfrith will give Wintermark a new national position, the Guardian of Dunfrith, elected by Wintermark's senators, who are not bound to choose Ham despite the announcement.

t.Hahnmark: Foresters of Woodhall in the southernmost reaches of Hahnmark cleared glades to establish the Dunfrith herb sinecure near Dunhearth Hall, including on old sites of skirmishes with the Feni.

r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: Wood Heath is the site of Dunfrith, where purpose-cut glades grow Bladeroot, Cerulean Mazzarine, Marrowort, True Vervain and Imperial Roseweald.

Construct Ministry in Sybella.d: Acting under the power to commission constructions delegated by the Senate, the Civilian Commissioner of Highguard approved a herb garden ministry in Sybella Cross costing fourteen wains of weirwood and 28 crowns in labour, taking three months to build. Rhesa, Exarch of Ravensfell, supplied the materials and money after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the sinecure creates the Highborn national title of High Herbalist of Sybella, expected to provide herbs at a preferential rate to the hospital. The holder is appointed by unanimous agreement of the Highguard senators and may be revoked by the Highguard national assembly, and also by the General Assembly and the Assembly of Nine.

n.Highguard: Highguard gains a new national title, the High Herbalist of Sybella, appointed by unanimous agreement of its senators and funded by Rhesa, Exarch of Ravensfell.

t.Bastion: Bastion is to gain a herb garden ministry, built over three months from fourteen wains of weirwood, which will supply herbs to the hospital at a preferential rate.

r.Bastion/Sybella Cross: Sybella Cross is the site of the new herb garden ministry, whose overseer will hold the title High Herbalist of Sybella.

Construct Ritual School of the White Sha.d: In Autumn 380YE the Civilian Commissioner of the Imperial Orcs used the legal power to commission constructions, delegated to them by the Senate, to approve a mana sinecure in Pakaanan's Pass, Skarsind. Its exact cost is not recorded, though standard costs apply. After the Autumn Equinox Yargol provided 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns towards the work. Once complete, the sinecure will create the title of Storm Shaman, a national title for the Imperial Orcs.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs' own Civilian Commissioner approved the project, and once finished it will give the nation a new national title, the Storm Shaman.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind, held by the Imperial Orcs, is to gain a mana sinecure, the Ritual School of the White Shaman, built within its borders.

r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Pakaanan's Pass is the chosen site for the Ritual School of the White Shaman, and Yargol's mithril and crowns went towards its construction there.

Construct herbal great work in Skarsind.d: Proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by Sermersuaq's senator, the motion took advantage of an opportunity that arose after Skarsind was assigned to the Imperial Orcs. The great work cost 45 wains of weirwood and 90 crowns in labour, and would take three months to construct. Bloodcrow Yargol provided the weirwood and the crowns after the Winter Solstice 380YE. Once complete, the work will provide 90 doses of True Vervain, split between the owners of herb gardens in Skarsind who attended the previous Anvil summit.

n.Imperial Orcs: The great work honours those orcs who never got to see a homeland. It was funded by Bloodcrow Yargol and will supply True Vervain to orc herb-garden owners in their newly assigned territory.

t.Skarsind: The great work is built in Skarsind. Once complete, it will distribute 90 doses of True Vervain among the territory's herb-garden owners who attended the previous summit.

Construct mana ministry in Astolat.d: Proposed by the Senator for Astolat and seconded by the Senator for Weirwater, the motion called for a mana ministry in Astolat whose position would be a lifetime appointment made by the Dawnish Senators. It passed in Autumn 380YE at an unrecorded cost, with standard costs applying. Some necessary details were missing from the motion, and the Senator for Astolat was allowed to decide them. Once completed, the ministry would have created a Dawnish national position. However, by the Autumn Equinox 381YE the commission had lapsed, so the ministry was never built.

n.Dawn: Dawn would have gained a national position appointed for life by its Senators, but this was lost when the commission lapsed by Autumn 381YE.

t.Astolat: Astolat was the proposed site of the mana ministry, and its Senator proposed the motion and was allowed to settle its missing details, though the commission lapsed before construction.

Construct the Celesti Lighthouse.d: Using construction powers delegated by the Senate, the Civilian Commissioner of the Brass Coast approved a motion to build the Celesti Lighthouse in Feroz for 16 wains of mithril. Its Keeper would be a Freeborn ministry appointed by the Brass Coast senators, empowered to buy mana directly from ships' captains at rates set by the civil service. The commission was announced after the maximum number of commissions had already been authorised, in case the Synod vetoed one of the earlier ones. The Synod did not use its veto, so the Celesti Lighthouse commission was not authorised and the lighthouse was not built.

n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn missed out on a ministry that their own senators would have appointed, with the power to buy mana from ships' captains, because the commission fell outside the season's authorised limit.

t.Feroz: Feroz would have gained the Celesti Lighthouse and its mana-buying ministry, but the commission was not authorised and no lighthouse was built there.

Construct the Colossus of Sarvos.d: Lorenzo 'La Volpe', Civilian Commissioner of The League, used the Senate's delegated power to commission constructions to approve the Colossus of Sarvos in Autumn 380YE. The great work was to be funded by the Bloody Butchers Guild and other loyal League citizens, and overseen by Lorenzo himself. Standard costs applied. After the Autumn Equinox, Lorenzo 'La Volpe' Macelliao von Temeschwar provided 40 wains of white granite and 10 thrones. Work finished shortly before the Winter Solstice 380YE. The Colossus provides additional income to every citizen who owns a business in Sarvos and attended the previous Anvil summit.

n.The League: The League's own Civilian Commissioner commissioned and personally funded this monument to Sarvos's liberation. League business owners in Sarvos who attend Anvil gain additional income from it.

t.Sarvos: The city of Sarvos gained the Colossus, a completed great work honouring its liberation and the citizens who died defending it, which boosts the income of businesses there.

Construct the Gardens of Pallas.d: Acting as Civilian Commissioner of Urizen, Juliana of Phoenix Reach approved the construction of a herb sinecure, the Garden of Pallas, in Zenith. The commission cost 20 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones in labour, with three months needed to build it. Juliana herself provided the weirwood and thrones after the 380YE Winter Solstice. Once built, the sinecure created the Urizen national title of Head Gardener of Urizen. The title was later amended by the Senate in Autumn 381YE.

n.Urizen: Urizen gained a new national title, Head Gardener of Urizen, commissioned and paid for by its own Civilian Commissioner, Juliana of Phoenix Reach.

t.Zenith: The Garden of Pallas, a herb sinecure, was built in Zenith, giving the territory the seat of the new Head Gardener of Urizen title.

Construct the Gardens of the Grim.d: Proposed by the senator for Karov and seconded by the senator for Volodmartz in Autumn 380YE, the motion sought to construct a herb sinecure in Miekarova named the Gardens of the Grim. Its holder, titled the Grim Gardener, was to be the repository of Chernebog's Chains, and the title was to be elected unanimously by the Varushkan senators. The motion failed, so the sinecure and title were not created.

n.Varushka: Varushkan senators for Karov and Volodmartz sought a Varushkan herb sinecure whose holder would be chosen unanimously by the nation's senators and hold Chernebog's Chains, but the proposal failed.

t.Miekarova: Miekarova was to be home to the Gardens of the Grim herb sinecure, but because the motion failed, nothing was built there.

Construct the Golden Fields.d: Acting under the power to commission constructions delegated to them by the Senate, the Civilian Commissioner of the Marches approved a mana sinecure in Hay, in the Golden Downs region of Mitwold. Its cost is not recorded, but standard costs apply. After the Spring Equinox 381YE Slias Merrick provided 10 mithril and 2 thrones towards the work. Once completed, the sinecure will create the Marcher national position of Keeper of the Golden Fields, a lifetime appointment made by the Marcher Senators.

n.The Marches: The Marches gain a new national position, the Keeper of the Golden Fields, which Marcher Senators will appoint for life once the sinecure is complete.

t.Mitwold: A mana sinecure was commissioned in Hay in Mitwold, and Slias Merrick provided 10 mithril and 2 thrones towards building it.

r.Mitwold/Golden Downs: The Golden Fields sinecure is to be built at Hay in Golden Downs, and its Keeper will be tied to this site.

Construct the Hanging Fruit Gardens of G.d: Using the power to commission constructions delegated by the Senate, the Civilian Commissioner of Navarr approved a great work, the Hanging Fruit Gardens of Gerondi, in Serenael in Miaren. It was to cost 40 wains of weirwood and 10 thrones in labour, taking three months to build. Once complete, it would have provided an additional 75 herbs each season, shared among the owners of herb gardens in Miaren who had attended the previous Anvil summit. The work was never completed: by the Autumn Equinox 381YE the commission had lapsed.

n.Navarr: Navarr's Civilian Commissioner approved this great work to boost herb production for Navarri herb gardeners in Miaren, but the commission lapsed before it was built.

t.Miaren: Herb garden owners in Miaren stood to share an extra 75 herbs from the planned gardens, a benefit lost when the commission lapsed in 381YE.

r.Miaren/Serenael: Serenael was chosen as the site of the Hanging Fruit Gardens of Gerondi, though construction never went ahead before the commission lapsed.

Construct the Pilgrim's Rest.d: Proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion authorised a self-funded sinecure costing ten wains of white granite and twenty crowns, taking three months to build. Once complete, it creates the Imperial title Crow Keeper of the Rest, carrying twelve votes in the Synod and six liao per season. The holder is appointed by the Wintermark National Assembly and may be revoked by that assembly, the General Assembly or the Assembly of Nine. Kitsana provided the granite and crowns after the Winter Solstice 380YE, allowing construction to proceed.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a national title, the Crow Keeper of the Rest, appointed by its National Assembly and carrying twelve Synod votes and six liao each season.

t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's senator proposed the sinecure, which is to be built within the territory once its materials are supplied.

r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: The Pilgrim's Rest is to be raised in Kallavesa Marsh from white granite supplied by Kitsana after the Winter Solstice 380YE.

Construct tomb for Empress Giselle.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Sarvos, the motion addressed the controversy over where Empress Giselle's remains should rest. It called for her body to be moved to Temeschwar and a tomb constructed there, with a Guardian of the Tombs appointed by the League national assembly who would receive liao and votes in the Synod. The motion passed. Ten wains of white granite and 20 crowns were provided towards the work, and the sarcophagus of Empress Giselle has been moved to Temeschwar. Once the tomb is complete, the sinecure will create the League national title of Guardian of Giselle's Tomb.

n.The League: The League gains custody of Empress Giselle's remains and, once the tomb is finished, a national title, Guardian of Giselle's Tomb, appointed by its national assembly and carrying liao and votes in the Synod.

t.Temeschwar: Empress Giselle's sarcophagus has been moved to Temeschwar, where her tomb is being built with granite and crowns provided towards the work, and it will be home to the new Guardian of Giselle's Tomb.

Disburse funds for rebuilding of Holmaue.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by the senator for Karov, sought funds for the rebuilding of the Holmauer in Holberg. It followed on from a previous motion to construct a park in Holmauer. The Senate passed it in principle and set the sum at 100 thrones. That money was then disbursed to the senator for Holberg.

n.The League: Holberg's senator, representing a League territory, proposed the motion and received the 100 thrones the Senate granted for rebuilding in Holmauer.

t.Holberg: Holberg's senator proposed the motion and was given 100 thrones for rebuilding works in the territory's Holmauer region.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holmauer was the subject of the motion, receiving 100 thrones for rebuilding, following an earlier motion to build a park there.

Disburse funds for resupply IV.d: The motion proposed disbursing funds to resupply the Imperial armies. It was proposed by Feroz and seconded by Kahraman, and passed in principle at a cost of 115 thrones 4 crowns, which was disbursed to Senator Feroz. The page notes that the motion did not give Senator Feroz the power to perform emergency resupply on the armies. It only provided the funds.

n.The Brass Coast: Two Brass Coast senators, those for Feroz and Kahraman, proposed and seconded the motion, and its 115 thrones 4 crowns went to the Feroz senator.

t.Feroz: The senator for Feroz proposed the motion and received the 115 thrones 4 crowns disbursed for resupplying the armies, though without any power to carry out emergency resupply.

Disloyal, unprosperous, unvigilant, unwi.d: The Private Auction had long caused debate, but opinion had generally favoured the status quo until four citizens were excommunicated for buying an item from it. Friar Alyn of Hay then travelled widely, preaching Prosperity and distributing pamphlets. He argued that the Synod's judgements calling citizens 'disloyal, unprosperous, unvigilant and unwise' were themselves unvirtuous, and that people should keep their artefacts or sell them personally. He claimed to have spoken to people in Astolat, Bastion, Skarsind and Meade, and drew enthusiastic crowds of corsairs in Siroc. Preliminary reports showed far fewer items offered for the Private Auction. Having finished his pilgrimage, Alyn announced he was coming to Anvil to address the Synod, chiefly the National Assembly of the Marches and the Assembly of Prosperity.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the friar claimed to have spoken to the seneschals of Astolat during his tour.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the friar claimed to have spoken to the benefactors of Bastion, and compared the Printer's Guild museum to something that would impress a Highborn archivist.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the friar claimed to have spoken to the bonesetters of Skarsind.
n.The Marches: The campaign came from a Marcher friar of Hay, who also claimed to have spoken to the stewards of Meade. He announced he would come to Anvil to address the National Assembly of the Marches in particular, alongside the Assembly of Prosperity.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the friar listed the seneschals of Astolat among those he had spoken to.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the friar listed the benefactors of Bastion among those he had spoken to.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold's town of Hay was home to Friar Alyn, whose preaching against selling treasures to the Bourse cut the Private Auction's prospectus.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the friar listed the bonesetters of Skarsind among those he had spoken to.

Empty skies (winds of magic).d: Since the Spring Equinox the night skies over Skarsind, Holberg, Necropolis, Bregasland and Segura have shown only the moon, the clouds and, in the north, the crimson star. Magicians cannot explain it; it does not resemble the Penumbral Veil. Shortly after the Summer Solstice it spread to Sermersuaq, Volodmartz, Karsk, Miekarova and the Barrens. Naga who spend long periods beneath these skies find their secretiveness greatly strengthened, needing real effort of will to answer directly or be honest. Separately, the Phoenix constellation, which had been fading from the sky and from magicians' memories, returned abruptly after the Solstice and is brighter than ever. The fog over the northern Bay of Catazar writhed for a night and vanished at dawn.

n.Druj: The Barrens, held by the Druj, fell beneath the empty, starless night sky shortly after the Summer Solstice.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Necropolis remained under the starless night sky, and naga lingering there grew markedly more secretive and evasive.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skarsind, held by the Imperial Orcs, continued to suffer empty night skies with no explanation from Imperial magicians.
n.The Brass Coast: Segura remained starless by night, strengthening the urge towards secrecy among naga who spent long periods there.
n.The League: Holberg's night skies stayed empty of stars, leaving the League's people beneath an eerie and unsettling darkness.
n.The Marches: Bregasland remained under the empty sky, with naga who stayed there finding honesty and directness a struggle.
n.Varushka: Varushka was hit hard as the phenomenon spread to three of its territories at once: Volodmartz, Karsk and Miekarova.
n.Wintermark: Sermersuaq joined the affected territories shortly after the Summer Solstice, its night skies emptied of stars.

t.Bay of Catazar: The supernatural fog that had shrouded the northern bay since Autumn 379YE writhed and glowed for a night, then boiled away within ten minutes of sunrise, leaving no trace.
t.Bregasland: Bregasland's night skies remained starless, unsettling those who studied them and deepening the secretiveness of naga who stayed there.
t.Holberg: Holberg continued to lie beneath an empty night sky showing only the moon and clouds.
t.Karsk: The empty sky spread to Karsk within days of the end of the Summer Solstice.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova's stars vanished shortly after the Summer Solstice as the phenomenon spread across Varushka.
t.Necropolis: The skies above Necropolis stayed starless, a darkness magicians remained unable to explain.
t.Segura: Segura's nights remained empty of stars, with naga who spent extended time there becoming markedly more secretive.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq newly fell under the empty sky after the Summer Solstice, leaving only the moon, clouds and the crimson star visible by night.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind remained one of the original starless territories, its night skies still empty.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens became affected shortly after the Summer Solstice, their night skies emptied of stars.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz was among the territories newly darkened shortly after the Summer Solstice, its stars vanishing from the night sky.

Fortify Foracci.d: The motion commissioned a fortification in the Foracci region of Sarvos. It cost 80 wains of white granite and 20 thrones in labour, would take a year to build, and needs 10 thrones a season in upkeep. Magdelena Alanga Di Sarvos supplied 20 wains of white granite after the Autumn Equinox 380YE, and a further 20 wains with the 20 thrones after the Winter Solstice 380YE. After the Autumn Equinox 381YE, Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar and Magdelena each gave another 20 wains, making up the full 80. When finished it will be a rank one fortification called "Our Lady of Pride".

n.The League: League senators for Sarvos and Tassato drove the motion, and League citizens, chiefly Magdelena Alanga Di Sarvos, provided most of the granite and money to strengthen the defences of a League city.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos gains a rank one fortification, "Our Lady of Pride", in Foracci. It was paid for largely by Sarvosan donations and costs 10 thrones a season to maintain.

r.Sarvos/Foracci: Foracci is the site of the new rank one fortification, "Our Lady of Pride", built from 80 wains of white granite over a year.

Goatfoot.d: For three months a horned, shaggy figure was sighted around Pakaanan's Pass, and occasionally in northern Northspires and eastern East Floes. At least a dozen mammoth carcasses were found near the Clattering Gulley, killed by apparent misfortune, then stripped of bones and tusks and their organs eaten. A week before the equinox the creature was identified as the Krampus, which curses those who confess crimes to it, the curse lasting until the next winter. It accosted caravans of the Crossroads of the North entering Skarsind, while expeditions sent to hunt it fell into disaster. It sought a compact with the Skarsind orcs, lamented that Burnlin Drum-Heart had not sent Runesmiths to carve the stones, wanted a hall of bones and a home before winter, and invited them to its camp. A Sentinel Gate conjunction would let eight people visit it.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Krampus addressed its message to the orcs as the new masters of Skarsind, offering to hear their sins and form a compact with the Skarsind tribe, and inviting them to its camp. One orc band that tried to hunt it suffered disaster.
n.Wintermark: The Krampus, previously associated with the Wintermark egregore, now seemed to seek a new home among the orcs, and lamented that Burnlin Drum-Heart had sent no Runesmiths to carve the stones. A Suaq hunting party that set out to challenge it met with ruin.

t.Hahnmark: The Krampus was occasionally seen in northern Northspires, though its activity centred on neighbouring Skarsind.
t.Sermersuaq: The Krampus was sometimes sighted along the eastern shores of the East Floes, and a Suaq hunting party that tried to challenge it ended in chaos and lasting injuries.
t.Skarsind: The Krampus made its camp above the Clattering Gulley, slaughtered mammoths in the area, accosted Crossroads of the North caravans entering the territory, and sought a compact with its new orc masters.

r.Hahnmark/Northspires: Northern Northspires saw occasional sightings of the Krampus during the three months before the equinox.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: The Krampus was occasionally spotted along the eastern shores of the East Floes.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: The Krampus lurked at Pakaanan's Pass, accosting travellers and merchants entering Skarsind while ignoring those leaving, and its camp above the Clattering Gulley became the target of a Sentinel Gate conjunction.

Iron and wine.d: Senator Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato oversaw 500 Thrones raised at Anvil, and private donors added more. The League's cities held a week of revelry in which Tassato turned the Vassa purple-and-gold with wine and gilding. Other nations held their own festivities, including a legendary Grand Tourney in Dawn. Foreign merchants and Summer and Night eternals joined in, though Sumaah stayed aloof. Inspired by the Empress' message, physicks and healing magicians now accompany every Imperial army, making the Steady Conquest order permanently available. The Senate was also offered a chance, open until the end of the 380YE Winter Solstice, to give one existing army the physick quality.

n.Dawn: Dawn held a Grand Tourney at the Castle of Thorns, said to be unmatched since Empress Richilde's day. Barien welcomed Dawn's nobles and yeomen to a Summer fair near the Semmerstones, and Dawn's weavers and war-witches were named among the battle-hardened healers.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard's herb masters are listed among the battlefield healers keen to help, and the Sumaah ambassador preached a sermon in Necropolis.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: in the story, the Jotun are described as a barbarian threat just over the horizon from the League.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr's herb masters are named among the battle-hardened healers eager to help the armies.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: in the story, two League potion-sellers rely on trade contacts in Feroz and Madruga.
n.The League: The League led the celebrations with a week of non-stop revelry in four cities and welcomed citizens of neighbouring nations. Its people produced art, a statue and a popular coronation song, and Senator Cesare took the lead in spending the celebration funds.
n.Urizen: Urizen marked the coronation with drifts of enchanted lightstones lighting the night sky, and its warmage healers are named among those eager to aid the armies.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's grimnir are named among the battle-hardened healers interested in helping the Empire.

t.Astolat: Despite the lingering curse on Astolat, Dawn's Grand Tourney was held on the fields around the Castle of Thorns, and troubadours claim it has never been matched.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the wine-and-gilt colouring of the Vassa reportedly reached as far south as the Sapphire Stair.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: in the story, two potion-sellers cite their contacts in Feroz as a source of supply for a planned military potion venture.
t.Holberg: Citizens of Holberg worked feverishly on a great frieze honouring the Empress, whom many see as a patron of their city, and the coronation song praises Holberg's walls.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: in the story, two potion-sellers cite their contacts in Madruga as a source of supply for a planned military potion venture.
t.Necropolis: Sumaah's ambassador stayed out of the festivities but preached a sermon in Necropolis, conceding that the Empire understands the role of celebration in the path of Prosperity.
t.Sarvos: In Caricomare the cursed statue of Mirislav mysteriously changed to show the ex-Senator smiling triumphantly with a coin and a lantern, and locals hailed it as another miracle.
t.Tassato: Under Prince Cesare's guidance, Tassato held extravagant celebrations, dyeing the Vassa purple-and-gold with red wine and Imperial Mint gilding, without undue violence between its two halves.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar unveiled a statue of Janon commissioned by Lorenzo La Volpe, prompting debate about public art in a city seen as dour. Vivier Iskander van Temeschwar's coronation song spread his name across the Empire.

r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Mestra competed with Regario to outdo the celebrations, decked in golden-horn bunting, and helped turn the Vassa purple-and-gold.
r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: Regario vied with Mestra in the revelry under red-fox bunting, contributing to the wine and gilding thrown into the Vassa.

Like a wheel within a wheel.d: The raid drove Grendel forces back from the Legacy. The Senate returned Spiral to Urizen control and elected Tanwyn Ankarien as its senator, with Edmundo of Endsmeet replacing her as Senator for Zenith. The Grendel still held Apulus, Ateri and, nominally, Screed, with a significant army. Personal resources reclaimed from the Grendel became spoils of war for the Military Council to allocate, among them the Ankarien Chess Set of thirty ushabti soldiers. The Legacy, mined again by ushabti and Urizen volunteers, became a national Bourse seat chosen by Urizen mana site owners. Recovering Spiral would not let Urizen support more armies. The Stonemasons offered to help build one cheap castle in Apulus or Apstrus, but only once all of Spiral was in Imperial hands. A report on further opportunities was expected by the Winter Solstice.

n.Grendel: The Grendel were pushed back from the Legacy and lost control of Spiral, though they still held three regions centred on Apulus and Ateri and kept a significant armed force there. Their continued presence was the condition holding back the Stonemasons' offer to build a castle.
n.Urizen: Spiral was returned to Urizen control under Senator Tanwyn Ankarien, and Urizen mana site owners would vote at the Autumn Equinox on who held the restored Legacy Bourse seat. The territory's sparse population meant its recovery would not let Urizen support any more armies.

t.Spiral: Spiral passed back into Imperial hands, yielding spoils of war such as the Ankarien Chess Set and a working Legacy mithril mine. Its remaining Grendel presence still left the territory volatile.

r.Spiral/Apstrus: Apstrus was one of the two sites the Stonemasons of Mezudan proposed for a castle, near the old heliopticon tower on the northern slopes, where it could deter attacks from the south and watch the unknown lands towards Axos.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Apulus remained a centre of Grendel control. It was also the Stonemasons' other proposed castle site, on the coast, where a fortress could resist Grendel naval assaults and control passes into the Broken Shore.
r.Spiral/Ateri: Ateri remained one of the two centres of Grendel control in Spiral.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: The Empire captured Ossuary after the Solstice raid, which gave it enough regions to take control of Spiral.
r.Spiral/Screed: Screed, where the Black Plateau squats, remained under nominal Grendel control.

Peace song.d: Lashonar's bird-like heralds sang in every tavern and inn across Dawn, lamenting the dead and urging peace with the Druj, who had sued for peace. All four Dawnish armies became a fifth less effective when attacking, though they defended normally. The civil service set out options: enmity, a Synod judgement to exterminate the heralds, a joint exclusionist response, or a Synod-backed peace in the Barrens. The Conclave removed Lashonar's amity without declaring enmity. The Dawnish National Assembly condemned the message and named Lady Tamain Sepulchre, backed by a hundred liao, to oppose it. She composed and popularised 'The Heralds of Lashonar'. The penalty applied through the autumn campaign but was gone by the Winter Solstice.

n.Dawn: The heralds' relentless songs sapped the morale of all four Dawnish armies, cutting their offensive effectiveness by a fifth for the autumn campaign. The National Assembly answered by sending Lady Tamain Sepulchre, whose counter-song ended the effect by the Winter Solstice.
n.Druj: Lashonar's heralds took up the cause of peace with the Druj, singing that those the Dawnish killed had come to sue for peace and offering to split the Barrens. The Synod was given the option of demanding an immediate peace with them, but the Empire chose to resist the eternal instead.

t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: an Earl consulted the weavers of Weirwater, who judged that the heralds' influence was not a spell as the Empire understands it but was magical in nature because Lashonar is a being of magic.

Pilgrimage.d: The message met confusion, curiosity and accusations of heresy, but a few in every land embraced it, and together they became a flood of pilgrims to Reikos, home of the Congregation of the First Empress, and Casinea, where Yael is rumoured to live. No living person had drawn such a following since Nicovar. By the Autumn Equinox Yael's congregation earned 160 votes and matching liao. The page set out opportunities: a Senate-authorised Sanctuary of the First Empress of white granite in Reikos or Casinea, with 10 wains donated by pilgrims; national assemblies spending liao to boost pilgrimage, possibly moving the movement's centre; or a General Assembly refutation backed by 500 liao.

n.Highguard: The pilgrimage centred on Highborn lands at Reikos and Casinea, with believers found in every Highborn chapter. Any sanctuary built there could have its priest appointed by the Highborn national assembly.
n.The League: A believer from each League street joined the pilgrimage, and merchants of every trade from the League swelled Yael's congregation.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: wagon raiders from Karsk are listed among the pilgrims flocking to hear Yael.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the hero-tombs in the marshes of Kallavesa are cited as an example of a traditional pilgrimage site.

t.Casinea: Pilgrims poured into Casinea, where Yael's personal congregation is said to live, and it was proposed as one possible site for the Sanctuary of the First Empress.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: in the accompanying story, a merchant had heard a street preacher in Holberg telling of the First Empress reborn.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: its marshes, where great heroes are interred, are named as an established place of pilgrimage.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: wagon raiders from Karsk are among the pilgrims travelling to see Yael.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the tombs of the Empresses and Emperors in Necropolis are cited as a traditional pilgrimage destination.
t.Reikos: Reikos, base of the Congregation of the First Empress and the centre of the new revelation, received a growing flood of pilgrims needing lodging and was proposed as the site of a sanctuary for them.

Song of the lakefolk.d: Hundreds of figures in dark animal skins, some emerging from the lake itself, gathered around a naked singer whose song spoke of theft, a lost lover and righting wrongs. They raided halls and houses, searching but neither stealing nor pressing attacks, fighting only when Winterfolk defended their homes, and refused all attempts at talk. Too small to be an army, they were nonetheless a nuisance, threatening to cost local farms and businesses 36 rings next season. Divination revealed nothing, though a conjunction near Atkonaroq was expected in Winter. Three Synod responses were offered; the Assembly of Wisdom, with some Wintermark National Assembly support, urged the people to learn about the Lakefolk, so the disruptive raids continued.

n.Wintermark: Winterfolk in the far north faced raids on their halls by the mysterious Lakefolk, and the Wintermark National Assembly lent some support to the Assembly of Wisdom's call to investigate, with Savik Summerstorm sent to coordinate.

t.Sermersuaq: The raiders camped on the northern shores of Lake Atkonaroq and kept searching local settlements, and because the chosen response focused on gathering knowledge rather than resisting them, farms and businesses in the territory continued to suffer disruption.

Starfall.d: The Stalker, a red star visible only in parts of the north, grew until it eclipsed other stars. Shooting stars carrying small amounts of ilium drew prospectors north, and three larger fragments fell in Kallavesa, Bregasland near Rushring, and West Ranging in Liathaven. The Senate and Conclave favoured diverting the star to Sküld under a peace agreement with the Thule, but Magistrate Abraham warned that someone must actually work the magic. Divinations showed it would otherwise hit Miekarova, devastating one region and costing every resource there improved beyond level one a level. Only spontaneous Autumn magic, worked in Miekarova or at the Anvil regio within a narrow window, could shift it. More ilium came to auction, and the star's strange influence on lineaged people and certain ailments ended.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Stalker was visible over Wickmoor and Sandling in Dawn's territory of Weirwater.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on the page and is linked only to the wider starfall.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Stalker could be seen in the northern sky over Skarsind.
n.Jotun: A large star fragment fell in the forests of West Ranging in Jotun-held Liathaven, and Imperial prospectors went searching for its ilium even in Jotun lands.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the star was visible over Hercynia, whose senator seconded the Senate statement on diverting the Stalker to Sküld.
n.The Marches: One of the three large star fragments struck Bregasland near Rushring, and the smoke and debris made the likely ilium bounty hard to locate.
n.Thule: Under the peace treaty, the Senate and Conclave backed using a Thule ritual to divert the Stalker onto Sküld, apparently by agreement with the northern orcs. The page notes that no one had yet actually worked the magic.
n.Varushka: The Stalker was visible across all of Varushka and was set to strike Miekarova, destroying one region and costing its improved resources a level, unless magic moved it. Volodmartz's senator proposed the diversion to Sküld.
n.Wintermark: A large star fragment fell in the marshes of Kallavesa, and the Stalker was visible over Sermersuaq and over Northspires and Bruckland in Hahnmark.

t.Bregasland: A large star fragment struck near Rushring, throwing up smoke and debris, and prospectors searched for what may be a significant bounty of ilium.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page and is linked only to the wider starfall.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the Stalker was visible in the skies over Northspires and Bruckland.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible over Hercynia, and its senator seconded the Senate statement on diverting the star.
t.Kallavesa: One of the three larger star fragments struck the marshes of Kallavesa, where its exact resting place was obscured but prospectors hunted for ilium.
t.Liathaven: A large star fragment fell in the deep forests of West Ranging, drawing Imperial prospectors into Jotun-held Liathaven in search of ilium.
t.Miekarova: Divinations showed the Stalker would land here during the Autumn Equinox, devastating one region and costing every resource improved beyond level one a level. Any ritual to divert it had to be worked here or at the Anvil regio.
t.Otkodov: The Senate and Conclave declared their wish to divert the Stalker onto Sküld under the peace treaty with the Thule, though the target region within the territory was not public.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Stalker was visible in the northern sky over Sermersuaq.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Stalker was visible in the northern sky over Skarsind.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: the red star could be seen over Wickmoor and Sandling.

r.Hahnmark/Bruckland: Mentioned in passing: Bruckland was one of the places where the Stalker could be seen.
r.Hahnmark/Northspires: Mentioned in passing: Northspires was one of the places where the Stalker could be seen.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: A large star fragment burned down into the deep forests here, leaving smoke and debris and drawing prospectors after its ilium.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Sküld was the Senate's and Conclave's chosen target for the diverted Stalker as part of the Thule peace treaty, though actually moving the star still required someone to work the magic.
r.Weirwater/Sandling: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible in the sky over Sandling.
r.Weirwater/Wickmoor: Mentioned in passing: the red star was visible in the sky over Wickmoor.

Thoughts are free (Trade Winds).d: The Sumaah Republic remained at war and Zemeh stayed closed, though dispatches still reached its embassy in Necropolis. Its Synod was considering the late Highborn Asher of Felix's Watch as a Paragon or Exemplar, while it claimed to hold the Imperial Crown and refused the Winter Solstice symposium unless it was wholly orthodox. Asavea resented delays to the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz, putting off any Temple of the Virtues in Nemoria until after Spring 381YE. The Commonwealth rescinded its extra tariffs but awaited concrete action. Jarm let its restrictions lapse and sent a negotiator. The Sarcophan Delves exchanged embassies with the Grendel. Axos invited Imperial traders after the Senate commissioned an embassy in Cargo.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Axou ships risking the Barren Sea approach could prove a boon to ports on the shores of the Semmerlak.
n.Grendel: The Grendel Salt Lords exchanged embassies with the Sarcophan Bedelaar Huisbaas, with Sarcophan diplomats opening one somewhere on the Broken Shore. Grendel pirates in the Bay of Catazar were seen as a threat to Axou merchants sailing to the Empire.
n.Highguard: The Sumaah kept sending dispatches to their embassy in Necropolis, and their Synod was considering naming the late Highborn Asher of Felix's Watch among their Paragons and Exemplars.
n.The Brass Coast: The delayed Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz soured Asavean feeling and pushed any trade benefits back to Spring 381YE at the earliest. Sarcophan merchants also made curious but seemingly unthreatening enquiries about the Krakenfire Armada, believed to be a Freeborn corsair family.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos and Tassato are named as ports from which Imperial captains set sail each season.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Meade is named as one of the Empire's ports sending trade ships abroad.
n.Urizen: The Senate had commissioned an Axou embassy in Cargo, near the Jarmish embassy, and Axos reciprocated by inviting Imperial civil servants to the Towers of Kantor.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Korotny is named as one of the Empire's ports sending trade ships abroad.

t.Bay of Catazar: The constant threat of Grendel pirates in the bay was expected to test whether Axou black-sailed merchant ships would brave the route to Imperial ports.
t.Feroz: Delays in completing the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull, and the Synod's opposition to it, angered the Asaveans and held up the proposed Temple of the Virtues in Nemoria.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Korotny is listed among the Imperial ports whose captains trade overseas.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Brass Coast ports such as Siroc and Lacre are listed among the Empire's trading harbours.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Meade is listed among the Imperial ports whose captains trade overseas.
t.Necropolis: The Sumaah embassy in Necropolis continued to receive diplomatic dispatches despite the ongoing war.
t.Redoubt: An Axou embassy had been commissioned in Cargo, not far from the Jarmish embassy, opening the way for trade with the citadels of Axos.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the ports from which brave captains set sail each season.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: as a territory on the Semmerlak, it could benefit if Axou merchants chose the Barren Sea approach.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the ports from which brave captains set sail each season.
t.The Semmerlak: Ports on the shores of the Semmerlak could gain substantially if Axou ships took the Barren Sea approach to avoid Grendel pirates.

Turbulence.d: Two days after the Summer Solstice a fierce thunderstorm struck the Semmerlak at sunset and battered fishing boats, costing catches and damaging some vessels. It ceased at dawn, leaving a windless day, then returned each night. Reports followed of hostile creatures active in the water after dark, named Semmerfolk or kalpie by the Dawnish and rusalka by the Varushkans. Fleets based in Semmerholm, Weirwater, Karov and Karsk faced a significant loss of production unless the problem was dealt with, and fisherfolk who rely on the lake were already suffering. The weather was clearly supernatural and seemed more than a simple curse. Magical investigation could target any of the four shore territories.

n.Dawn: Dawnish fleets in Semmerholm and Weirwater faced serious losses, yeomen and noble houses fishing the lake were already hurt, and the Dawnish named the attacking creatures Semmerfolk or kalpie.
n.Druj: Sailors reported that the storms battered the eastern shores of the Semmerlak just as hard as elsewhere, so the Druj in the Mallum were presumably suffering as well.
n.Varushka: Varushkan fleets in Karov and Karsk faced significant losses, and Varushkans named the predatory creatures in the water rusalka.

t.Karov: Fleets based in Karov faced a significant penalty to production unless the turbulence was dealt with, and Karov was one of the shore territories through which magical investigation could be made.
t.Karsk: Fleets based in Karsk were hampered by the nightly storms and windless days, and Karsk could serve as a target for magical investigation into the phenomenon.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm's fleets and fisherfolk were troubled by the storms and lake creatures, and the territory could be targeted to investigate the supernatural weather.
t.The Semmerlak: The lake itself suffered calm days and violent stormy nights, with monstrous creatures hunting its waters after dark. Because it is not a territory, it could only be investigated through the territories along its shores.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater's fleets faced a significant loss of production and its fisherfolk were hurt by the turbulence, and the territory was a possible focus for magical investigation.

When all this was trees.d: Weary and depleted after seasons fighting Imperial forces around Dawnguard, the orcs raised a great camp in the Lower Tarn Valley. Their young chief and experienced council insist on keeping their own culture and faith, and they rebuffed approaches from Therunin guides. Their army needs 50 Thrones a season after the Winter Solstice and wants weirwood or mithril to rearm. It will defend Therunin against the Druj but commits to nothing else. They asked the Empire to cede the Upper Tarn Valley, Lower Tarn Valley or Eastring to their own law. Unidentified briars accompany them. Caerwyn Summercrow gave them 50 Thrones, but they remain in makeshift camps awaiting an answer on land.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the orcs' depleted numbers are blamed on seasons of fighting Imperial forces in and around Dawnguard in the Barrens.
n.Druj: The Great Forest orcs pointedly distance themselves from the Druj and their slave-keeping. Their warchief would fight alongside the Navarr if the Druj invaded Therunin.
n.Navarr: The Navarr of Therunin are hosting thousands of foreign orcs at their Senator's invitation. They are being asked to give up one of their northern regions, and they are the people the orcs' delegation wishes to speak to at Anvil.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Senate's earlier support for the Hierro clan orcs in Segura is cited as a precedent for funding the Great Forest army.

t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the previous arrangement with the Hierro clan orcs in Segura is given as a model for Senate support of a foreign orc army.
t.The Barrens: The Great Forest orcs abandoned the Barrens, where they had fought Imperial forces, and may have brought with them briars suspected to be anarchists of Dourfell Keep.
t.Therunin: Therunin now hosts the Great Forest orcs and their army, and they have asked for one of its three northern regions under their own law. With the vallorn holding Sweetglades and Greenheart, ceding a region would leave the Empire only a single region short of losing the territory.

r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Mentioned in passing: the orcs were worn down by several seasons of fighting Imperial forces in and around Dawnguard.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: The Great Forest orcs' army and most of their nation left the Barrens through Hope's Rest on their way into the Tarn Valley.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Eastring is one of the three northern regions the orcs have asked the Empire to cede to their control.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's presence in Greenheart is noted as already reducing Navarr control of Therunin.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The orcs' great camp was raised here, and they remain in makeshift camps. The region is also one of the three they have asked to be given.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's presence in Sweetglades is noted as already reducing Navarr control of Therunin.
r.Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley: The Upper Tarn Valley is one of the three northern regions the orcs have asked to be ceded to their own law.

Will to survive.d: Whittle's friars, aided by liao donated to Whittle folk staying in Overton, began dedicating converts to Hatred, and hallowed weapons and consecrated campfires appeared across the Mournwold. A Statement of Principle backing Hatred of the Jotun, with a named priest providing 50 liao each season, would make every Mournwold region easier to retake by fostering resistance, though magistrates warned of possible condemnation for religious crimes. A rival statement denouncing Hatred, backed by 25 liao, would halt it but could push young Marchers to fight for the Jotun. The Drakes, Granite Pillar, Strong Reeds, Tusks and Winter Sun could use the "Into the Abyss" order while fighting in the Mournwold.

n.Jotun: Their newly conquered hold on the Mournwold faced Marcher resistance fuelled by Hatred, which could make every region easier for the Empire to retake, and Imperial armies could choose to fight them with an order that rejected the Jotun's rules of honourable engagement.

t.Mournwold: Now wholly under Jotun control, the territory became the centre of Whittle's preaching of Hatred, with hallowed weapons and consecrations spreading among its people and the soldiers fighting there. Depending on the Synod's choice, it would either become easier to retake or see more young Marchers take up arms for the Jotun.

r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Mentioned in passing: Marcher-folk who yearned to stand on the hills of Freemoor again were described as grieving the fall of the Mournwold.
